questions.question: A stone is projected from the ground with velocity 25 {~m} / {s} . Two seconds later, it just clears a wall 5 {~m} high. The angle of projection of the stone is ({g}=10 {~m} / {sec}²)

questions.question: A particle is projected horizontally with a speed of 20/√(3) {~m} / {s} , from some height at {t}=0 . At what time will its velocity make 60^{} angle with the initial velocity ?
questions.explanation: tan60∘=VyVx Since tan60∘=3, we have: 3=VyVx Substitute Vy and Vx: 3=gt203 Rearranging gives: 3×203=gt Simplifying:20 = 10t From the equation 20 = 10t : t=2010=2 seconds

questions.question: A student is able to throw a ball vertically to a maximum height of 40 {~m} . The maximum distance to which he can throw the ball in the horizontal direction is :
questions.explanation: For vertical throw: H=u²2g=40H=u²/2g=40 So, u²=80gu²=80g Maximum horizontal range: Rmax=u²g=80gg=80 m

questions.question: A projectile fired with initial velocity u at some angle θ has a range R. If the initial velocity be doubled at the same angle of projection, then the range will be
If the initial velocity of a projectile be doubled, keeping the angle of projection same, the maximum height reached by it will
During projectile motion, acceleration of a particle at the highest point of its trajectory is
The maximum range of a projectile is 22 {~m} . When it is thrown at angle of 15^{} with the horizontal, its range will be-
questions.explanation: Given the maximum range Rmax =22 m at θ=45° we use the formula Rmax =v²g to find the initial velocity v. Rearranging the formula, we get v²=Rmax⋅g Substituting Rmax=22 m and g=9.8 m/s2 we get v²=22×9.8=215.6. Thus, v=215.6≈14.68 m/s. Now, we calculate the range R at θ=15° using the formula R=v²sin(2θ)g Substituting v=14.68 m/s,θ=15°, and g=9.8 m/s2, we get R=(14.68)2sin30°9.8. Since sin30°=0.5, we have R=215.6×0.59.8=107.89.8=11 m

questions.question: A bullet is fired horizontally from a rifle at a distant target. Ignoring the effect of air resistance, which of the following is correct? Horizontal Acceleration,Vertical Acceleration
questions.explanation: Ignoring air resistance, the only force acting on the bullet after it leaves the rifle is gravity. Hence, horizontal acceleration is zero: ax = 0 Vertical acceleration is due to gravity: ay = g ≈ 10 m/s² Therefore, Horizontal Acceleration = 0 Vertical Acceleration = 10 m/s²
